findings.pdf_says: When an operand is textually subscripted, as operand-j<sub>n</sub>, the term 'operand-j' identifies a specific operand and 'n' refers to the nth position or occurrence of operand-j.
findings.markdown_says: When an operand is textually subscripted, as operand-jn, the term 'operand-j' identifies a specific operand and 'n' refers to the nth position or occurrence of operand-j.
findings.why_it_matters: The subscript n is printed as a subscript in the PDF; the markdown flattens it to 'operand-jn', so the very notation 5.3.1 defines is not shown (it reads as a different operand name).

findings.why_it_matters: Table 1 aligns each alternative expression with its verbal form (e.g. 'is not permitted' is the alternative for 'shall not', 'is not required to' for 'need not', and 'should not' / 'cannot' have none). The markdown collapses each row's forms and alternatives into undivided lists, so which alternative expression is equivalent to which verbal form (positive vs negative) is lost.
